answer: Each AI grader is assigned to a random ridge of the network’s reputation ledger, where its identity hash is anchored to a verifiable proof‑of‑work “ledge” stake. Periodically a peer jury draws a pearl‑coded sample of graders from across ridges and runs spot‑check audits; any mismatch triggers slashing of the stake and broadcast of the offender’s hash. An attacker must thus acquire enough ledge stake on every ridge to survive audits, inflating the cost linearly with the number of ridges targeted.
